newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-CANDELORO DREAMS OF AN IMPERIAL SEASON.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-CANDELORO DREAMS OF AN IMPERIAL SEASON.

text.p: Olympic medallist Philippe Candeloro hopes to restore some pride to French figure skating by impersonating Napoleon Bonaparte on ice.

Candeloro, the 1994 Olympic bronze medallist, may be taking a risk as Napoleon's only contact with ice was probably the 1812 Russian retreat, one of the most disastrous military campaigns in French history.
But Candeloro, who hopes to return to the rink next month after a season marred by poor results and injury, has had enough ups and downs in his career to be cautious.
"My programme will not go as far as showing Napoleon's death. It will stop at the victories like Austerlitz and will not mention defeats such as Waterloo," he said.
The Frenchman has had his own personal defeats in the past. Acting as the Godfather, he showed he was was one of the best skaters in the world.
But in his last programme as cartoon cowboy Lucky Luke, Candeloro bit the dust.
The hiccups have not hampered his ambitions.

"Napoleon was a great man and, without boasting, I would like to be like him someone important in France, to leave my mark in figure skating like he left his in French history," he told a news conference at the Lalique Trophy competition.
Candeloro said he thought he looked a bit like the Emperor.
"He was short like me. He had a strong bearing...and I'm trying to look the same. I hope someday someone will try to emulate me," he said.
Candeloro has all the more reason for staging a comeback -- as Napoleon did in 1815 after being sent into exile -- as next January's European championships will be held in Paris.
His programme will contain eight triple jumps and two double axels and his music will include excerpts from the French national anthem, La Marseillaise.
"It is a programme that should appeal to France and I hope to snatch a gold medal," he said.
Out of action since May after an operation on his right ankle, Candeloro hopes to return in next month's NHK Trophy in Japan.
"For the first time since my operation I can skate without feeling any pain. If I can train like this for two weeks I'll be ready", he said.
